Plugin Reference Overview

This page gives the overall picture of the SA plugin system: how plugins are declared, how they are installed, and which plugins this chapter covers. After reading it, you can judge which plugin should provide a given capability (networking, database, UI, runtime) and which page to consult for details. Note: basic cores such as networking are already built into sa_std (see the architecture principle below); they are not provided by plugins.

Version statusAs of 2026-10-19, the 0.17 branches of all plugin repositories covered in this chapter (sax, react, mui, vite, tui, wgpu, 3dengines, vm, sla, deno, node, bun, pkg, http-client, http-server, db, bc2sa) have completed the Zig 0.17 migration: they build with Zig 0.17, pass the Zig unit tests, and have been verified for installation with sa plugin install --dev (0.17 branch; sci corresponds to main). The old 0.14.1 branches are kept unchanged.
Architecture principle (2026-10-24) All basic cores are built into sa_std, without exception. Plugins only wrap interface usage habits (API familiarity and ergonomics); that does not mean substance/capability may be pushed down into plugins. The HTTP/1.1 client and server, HTTP/2, WebSocket, TCP/UDP, QUIC/HTTP3, TLS fingerprint shaping, SSH (client and server), multipart parsing and building, gzip/deflate/brotli and other cores all live in sa_std (sci src/runtime/, declared in sa_std/*.sai): you can do everything without installing any plugin; a plugin is never a capability gate. The plugins covered in this chapter are the framework layer and ecosystem facades on top of these cores (such as vite orchestration and the deno/node/bun compatibility layers); their value is ease of use, not capability itself. For pages involving core capabilities, the sa_std declarations are authoritative.

What an SA plugin is

An SA plugin is a dynamic-library project (built with Zig, producing artifacts such as libdb.so / tui.dll) carrying a manifest file sap.json. It exposes native capabilities to SA programs through the C ABI and @extern/.sai contracts, and can also register new CLI subcommands (such as sa vm run and sa sax build).

Key fields of sap.json (schema sa.plugin/1):

FieldDescription
name / versionPlugin name and version (currently all 0.1.0)
abiPlugin ABI version and the required saasm version, e.g. >=0.4.0
skillsThe capability segment names declared externally, viewable with sa skills --json, e.g. http.server, tui.input
permissionsDeclarative permission ledger: fs / net / env / process.spawn and an exec whitelist
dependenciesDependencies on other plugins (including version, ABI, local path, and an optional symbol subset symbols)
interfacesContract files facing SA: .sai (extern declarations) and .sal (macro facades)
NotePlugins are optionally installed: before use, confirm installation with sa plugin list and confirm the capability segments are loaded with sa skills --json; do not assume a given plugin necessarily exists. Development-time installation uniformly goes through --dev:
# 在插件目录内执行；依赖会按 sap.json 一并安装
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa plugin install --dev .
sa plugin list          # 查看已安装插件
sa skills --json        # 查看已加载的能力段

Some plugins are blocked in production run mode because they declare broad permissions, and need SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 for local trusted verification (such as vm).

Quick classification

  • UI / graphics: sax, react, mui, vite, tui, wgpu, 3dengines — in-depth UI usage belongs to the "SAX / MUI UI Development" chapter; this chapter only goes as far as "what it can do and how to enable it".
  • Runtime / language access: vm (interpreter), sla (compiler), bc2sa (bitcode migration entry point), pkg (the main dependency-management entry point).
  • System / network / data: http-client, http-server, deno, node, db.
WarningAll plugins are in the early 0.1.0 form: APIs may change breaking-ly (for example, db has removed the old direct-query ABI); the README of each plugin repository and its sap.json / .sai files are authoritative.
